The acquisition will see the open-source of Gitter's code, and the launch of a new feature called Topics, which allows users to ask and answer questions similar to Stack Overflow. Gitter was founded in 2014, and has since attracted over 800,000 developers. Three of Gitter's six employees will join GitLab, while its cofounders will remain in London. GitLab continues to offer Mattermost as an alternative to the proprietary Slack app for internal team communication.

Gitter provides chat rooms linked to repositories of code for collaboration, and it has been popular on both GitLab and its main competitor, GitHub. As part of GitLab, Gitter is launching a new feature called Topics for Q&A, similar to Stack Overflow. The deal terms were not disclosed, and the integration of Gitter into GitLab's community and enterprise editions is yet to be announced. Gitter was launched in 2014 and has around 300,000 monthly active users. The acquisition follows a $20 million funding round for GitLab in September. GitLab continues to recommend the open-source Mattermost software as an alternative to the proprietary Slack app for internal team communication.

Genius, a media company once focused on annotating the internet, has undergone significant changes. After laying off a quarter of its staff, primarily engineers, in January, the company is shifting resources towards video content and distribution, aiming to become more video-focused as a media company. This move aims to make knowledge more accessible and attract a wider audience, particularly beyond the music world. The company continues to hire for roles in video and sales, and has redesigned its homepage to accommodate editorial content and advertising. Genius' shift from an all-encompassing internet annotator to a traditional media company model is more dramatic than most, as it competes with numerous well-capitalized competitors in the video market.
